record.context_brief: noncommuting polynomial recurrence with extra variable
record.original_question: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure preserving transformations, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Must every measurable set A of positive measure contain a pattern of the form A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)} A with positive measure for some m, n ∈ N?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let (X, X , µ) be a probability space, T1, . . . , Tℓ : X → X be invertible measure preserving transformations, and p1, . . . , pℓ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Show that for every A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0 we have µ(A ∩ T1^m+p1(n) A ∩ · · · ∩ Tℓ^m+pℓ(n) A) > 0 for some m, n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell:X\to X$ be (not necessarily commuting) invertible measure-preserving transformations. Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[n]$ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Prove or disprove: for every $A\in\mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A)>0$ there exist $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{\,m+p_1(n)}A\cap T_2^{\,m+p_2(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{\,m+p_\ell(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Frantzikinakis (2013, published 2023) established the desired multiple recurrence (in fact a positive lower bound on the averages) when the polynomials p_1,...,p_ℓ are rationally independent and have zero constant term, for arbitrary invertible measure-preserving T_i. However, in 2025 counterexamples were produced showing that double recurrence (ℓ=2) can fail for non-commuting transformations when the p_i are injective polynomials of equal degree (degree 1, or both degree ≥2), so the general problem as stated does not always hold. Thus the question is partially resolved: positive results exist under rational independence, while the unrestricted problem has been disproved in certain cases.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence for non-commuting transformations along rationally independent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple recurrence result for arbitrary measure-preserving transformations along polynomials of the form m+p_i(n) with rationally independent p_i having zero constant term.
status_evidence.claim: Positive answer under the additional hypothesis that the polynomials are rationally independent.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to double recurrence for non-commuting deterministic transformations
status_evidence.snippet: For p_1,p_2 injective integer polynomials vanishing at 0 with both degree 1 or both degree ≥2, double recurrence fails for non-commuting, mixing, zero-entropy transformations.
status_evidence.claim: The unrestricted version of the problem fails in certain non-commuting settings.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence without commutativity
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of Frantzikinakis's results on non-commuting multiple recurrence with the extra averaging variable m.
status_evidence.claim: The two-parameter (m,n) formulation circumvents the obstructions to single-variable polynomial recurrence in the non-commuting setting.
